subject: botany
question_text: Give a brief account of prothallus.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack botany section, Chapter 4 Plant Kingdom, book p.9, SAQ 6. The book's answer is a bullet list with no figure; the labelled heart-shaped prothallus sketch is added here as the exam-standard support for a 4-mark 'brief account' — its 1 mark in the split is therefore this card's claim, not the book's. Only one source book is held for botany — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand is physics-only and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card, not merely unrun. The whole split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

steps.label: Definition
steps.why: Every word of the definition is a marked point: haploid (the spores come from meiosis), multicellular, free-living (independent of the sporophyte), photosynthetic and thalloid.
common_mistakes: Calling the prothallus a sporophyte — it is the gametophyte generation.
Writing that it is unicellular — the prothallus is multicellular.
steps.memory_tip: Pro-thallus = the simple thallus stage that comes before the fern plant you see.
steps.margin_note: The boxed line plus one full sentence earns this mark.

steps.label: Labelled diagram
steps.why: A heart-shaped outline with rhizoids and the two sex organs marked is the exam-standard sketch: archegonia sit near the apical notch, antheridia among the rhizoids near the pointed end.
common_mistakes: Placing archegonia and antheridia at the same spot — archegonia lie near the notch, antheridia among the rhizoids.
Leaving the labels off — an unlabelled sketch earns little.
steps.memory_tip: Heart shape, notch up: the egg organs sit near the notch; the swimming-gamete organs sit low, among the rhizoids.
steps.margin_note: A 3-minute labelled sketch; these four labels are enough.

steps.label: Growth requirements
lines: The prothallus needs cool, damp, shady
places to grow, and water for the
antherozoids to swim to the archegonia.
spread of ferns to moist habitats.
steps.why: The gametophyte has no roots or vascular tissue, and its fertilisation needs a film of water — so the whole fern life cycle stays tied to moist places.
common_mistakes: Writing dry or sunny places — cool, damp and shady is the marked phrase.
steps.memory_tip: Three growth words together: cool, damp, shady — plus water for fertilisation.
steps.margin_note: The NCERT phrase 'cool, damp, shady' carries this mark.

steps.label: Sex organs
lines: In heterosporous ones, the male and
steps.why: The prothallus is the sexual stage of the fern life cycle: it carries the antheridia and archegonia. Whether both sit on one prothallus depends on homospory versus heterospory.
common_mistakes: Writing that the fern plant itself bears the sex organs — they form only on the prothallus, the gametophyte.
steps.memory_tip: One spore type → one prothallus with both organs; two spore types → two separate gametophytes.
steps.margin_note: The boxed line plus the homosporous/heterosporous contrast completes the answer.

insider_note: Definition, diagram, growth needs and sex organs are four short parts — students who write only the definition leave three marks behind.
